description: Lossless bounded block. Decode every {$ref:N} from shared_values[N] (fully expanded, one lookup). quote_span_table rows: [start,end,original_quote_type,original_quote_metadata]. Each SAME-entry attached_verbatim_passage_spans_ids and answer_quotation_spans_ids references table rows in order; exact quote is full supplied summary[start:end], Unicode half-open. Original object/string metadata retained; __transport_text_field__ names text/verbatim field, remove it on restoration. Span sha256_utf8 reconstructs as SHA256 of exact quote. answer_transport joins restored answer_quotations. All original raw fields/quotes/numeric/case fields reconstruct exactly. No keys or answers outside this fixed block supplied. No cross-entry or cross-reader borrowing.

rubric.correct: Every actually requested fact correct, resolved and summary-supported; equivalent complete meaning accepted; no material contradiction.
rubric.partial: Missing/unresolved requested fact with no material contradiction.
rubric.incorrect: Any material contradiction, including volunteered contextual claims.

global_constraints: No borrowing a fact from another question or reader.
Do not require ancillary source-only facts or contextual key facts excluded here.
Named board order may convey an order without listing every suit.
A clear operational equivalent passes without parroting key wording.
Semantic relation must be present: one user is not once total; paid use is not necessarily user pays; global three Visions is not personal draws; one unmatched site card is not all unmatched.
Free Chronicle together with affirmative Exile-winner permission may convey normal-offer waiver.
This file does not certify source audit or silently fix a fixed expected answer.

questions.question: An attack-die pool is empty and a battle plan removes an attack die. What happens? Which battle plans do bandits use and in what sequence do sides choose plans?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: For each removal from empty attack pool,add defense die. Attacker chooses ruled plans once each then defender; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. Plan resources do not block paying its plan cost.

required_facts.expected_fact: Each such removal instead adds one defense die.
Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender.
Bandits use all ruled no-cost plans.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Occupied plan can still be paid.

questions.question: After skulls leave an attacking force of five warbands, the attacker loses. How many die and where do survivors go? Does winning defender take attacker’s relics?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Kill half remaining force rounded down:two,leaving three on attacker board. Only victorious attacker resolves declared targets; winning defender takes no attacker relics. Skulls already removed before halving.

required_facts.expected_fact: Kill two (half rounded down), leaving three survivors on attacker board.
No; only victorious attacker resolves declared targets.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Premise already specifies five after skulls; arithmetic must use five, but no separate narration of earlier skull timing is required.

numeric_application.given_state: Five attacking-force warbands remain after skulls; attacker then loses.
numeric_application.completed_events: Skull casualties are already removed. Resolve defeat loss from the remaining force.

completed_events: Skull casualties have already been removed.
Apply the attacker-loss half-force casualty rule.

questions.question: A defender’s pawn is away from attacker and every targeted site. Do board warbands defend, and do warbands at untargeted sites defend? How are shield doubles applied?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: No board force unless pawn at attacker/targeted site; only targeted-site garrisons add,not untargeted sites. Doubles multiply rolled shields exponentially,not warband defense. No intrinsic warband defense dice.

required_facts.expected_fact: No board warbands defend when pawn is at neither attacker nor targeted sites.
Only targeted-site garrisons contribute; untargeted garrisons do not.
Multiply rolled shields exponentially, not warband defense.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Warbands do not inherently contribute defense dice.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Question asks force contribution and shield multiplication, not dice-pool composition.

questions.question: Are warbands, favor, secrets and dice component-limited? If a requested gain exceeds a source, what is done, and can you intentionally burn extra resources?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Warbands/favor/cards limited; secrets/dice unlimited. Gain/take maximum possible from source,not more; boards/banks no cap unless specified. Cannot place/burn/sacrifice beyond prompted cost/requirement.

required_facts.expected_fact: Warbands/favor limited; secrets/dice unlimited.
Take/gain as much as available, not beyond source.
Cannot place/burn/sacrifice beyond prompted cost/requirement.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Storage capacity is separate from source exhaustion and is not asked.

questions.question: Which game information is private and public? May a holder show a facedown adviser or lie about its identity?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Private facedown fronts,discard fronts,world-deck count and backs beyond top. Public all else including discard counts/backs and board favor,secrets,warbands. Holder may peek/show facedown adviser and players may lie about private info; cannot mix advisers indistinguishably.

required_facts.expected_fact: Private: facedown fronts, discard fronts, world-deck count and backs below top.
All else public, including discard counts/backs and board favor/secrets/warbands.
Holder may inspect/show it; players may lie about private identity.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Do not mix facedown advisers indistinguishably.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Physical tracking rule is not private/public classification or permission to show/lie.

questions.question: How do must, cannot, ignore and must-if-able interact; which book takes priority; do a Give restriction and a Take restriction mean the same thing?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Cannot beats must,which beats ordinary; ignore overrides specifically named must/cannot. Must-if-able fulfilled when possible,otherwise no penalty. Law beats Playbook/aids except Site Reference,nonitalic beats reminder. Give/Take distinct; restricting one does not change other.

required_facts.expected_fact: Must beats ordinary; cannot beats must; ignore overrides specified must/cannot.
Must-if-able performs when possible, otherwise no penalty.
Law over Playbook/aids except Site Reference.
Distinct keywords; restricting one does not automatically restrict the other.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Within-text typography priority is separate from requested book precedence.

questions.question: Are ordinary promises or free resource gifts binding/legal? What exceptions exist, including Reliquary relics and Tribunal?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Ordinary promises nonbinding; unprompted resource transfer not authorized. Citizenship and powers saying binding bind agreed listed things if able. Only Citizenship offer can exchange Reliquary relic; Tribunal binding favor/secrets and future actions,disputed breach coin flip.

required_facts.expected_fact: Ordinary promises nonbinding; unprompted resource transfers not authorized.
Citizenship/powers expressly binding require agreed listed exchanges if able.
Only Citizenship offer may exchange Reliquary relic.
Permits binding immediate favor/secrets and future actions; disputed future breach by coin flip.

questions.question: What happens when each of the four Reliquary spaces is uncovered for Chancellor: Brutal, Decadent, Careless and Greedy?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Brutal: when Chancellor attacker,defeated player even self kills all force. Decadent: travel Provinces/Hinterland→Cradle no Supply; to Hinterland +1 Supply. Careless: Trade gains one extra favor even secret trade; secret trade gains one fewer secret. Greedy: draw two extra on Search,still stops at world Vision,cannot Search if cost >2 Supply. Mandatory uncovered modifiers.
questions.source_references: Law setup illustration; Playbook p3 Reliquary

required_facts.expected_fact: When Chancellor attacks, defeated player even Chancellor kills all force.
Provinces/Hinterland→Cradle no Supply; Travel to Hinterland +1.
Trade gains one additional favor even secret trade; secret trade yields one fewer secret.
Draw two additional Search cards; cannot Search costing over two Supply.
Uncovered modifiers mandatory for Chancellor.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Greedy still stops on world Vision.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Unchanged ordinary Search stop behavior is context to what the uncovered modifier changes; not an independent extra recital.

questions.question: Which winner can build or repair an edifice in Chronicle, how many, where, and may a new edifice replace a denizen at a site already holding a ruin?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Only Chancellor/Citizen winner,one build or repair. Build at ruled site with no edifice intact or ruined,replace matching denizen by intact Archive edifice,denizen to world deck. Or repair ruled ruin by flipping intact. No building over an existing ruin.

required_facts.expected_fact: Chancellor/Citizen winner may build or repair one.
At ruled site with neither intact nor ruined edifice, replace matching denizen with intact Archive edifice; denizen returns world deck.
Cannot build over existing ruin.
At ruled site flip a ruin intact.

questions.question: In Chronicle, which sites are discarded, where do their attached cards go, and what happens to retained sites with intact edifices not ruled by winner?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Discard sites unless winner rules or intact edifice exists;shuffle sites into deck,denizens to discard,relics to relic deck,ruined edifices Archive. At retained non-winner sites flip intact edifices to ruins; this ruining step discards denizens only at sites where an intact edifice actually flipped to ruin. Set aside all ruin sites with attached ruin,denizens,relics in map order; remove all pawns/resources/warbands from map.

required_facts.expected_fact: Discard sites except those winner rules or containing intact edifice.
Sites shuffled into site deck; denizens discard; relics relic deck; ruined edifices Archive.
Flip retained non-winner intact edifices to ruins; this ruining step discards denizens only at sites where an intact edifice actually flipped to ruin.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Set aside all ruin sites with attachments in map order.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Subsequent map-packing/refill preparation not asked by discard/retained-edifice clauses.
Later piece cleanup not among asked card destinations.

questions.question: Give the ordered Chronicle process for filling empty map slots, including the reverse ordering of ruins and faceup-site guarantee.
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Non-ruins: fill Cradle top-down with Cradle then Provinces then Hinterland top-down; Provinces top-down push then import Hinterland; push Hinterland up. Ruins saved in top-to-bottom order then place bottom-up into Hinterland bottom-up,then Provinces bottom-up. Fill remaining slots facedown from site deck; flip top site in regions with no faceup site.

required_facts.expected_fact: Cradle top-down: push Cradle, import Provinces then Hinterland top-down.
Provinces top-down: push then import Hinterland; push Hinterland up.
Saved ruins top-to-bottom; insert bottom-up into Hinterland bottom-up then Provinces bottom-up.
Fill remaining slots facedown from site deck; flip top site in any region with no faceup site.

questions.question: How are six Archive cards selected for world deck in Chronicle, including suit ties and no suited advisers?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Winner most common adviser suit,choose tied suit or any if no suited advisers;three random cards of it,two next clockwise,one next. Clockwise Discord→Arcane→Order→Hearth→Beast→Nomad→Discord.

required_facts.expected_fact: Winner’s most common suited adviser suit; choose tied suit or any suit with no suited advisers.
Three random Archive cards of chosen suit, two next clockwise, one next clockwise in printed suit/bank order.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Naming the printed clockwise order is an equivalent specification; no separate memorized-list criterion if that order is clear.

questions.question: If Archive cannot supply the Chronicle’s required 3/2/1 cards, is a partial allocation added, and how is the Archive healed?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Do not add normal allocation. Take all Dispossessed,sort six suit stacks,take six random from largest stack into world deck,shuffle each remaining Dispossessed suit stack into matching Archive stack.

required_facts.expected_fact: Do not add the normal allocation partially.
Sort all Dispossessed into suit stacks; take six random from largest stack into world deck.
Shuffle remaining Dispossessed of each suit into matching Archive stack.

questions.question: What cards are eligible to become Dispossessed during Chronicle, how many are removed, and what happens to Visions and winner’s advisers?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Set aside all five Visions including Conspiracy. Shuffle all region discards with losing players advisers;take six random unseen into Dispossessed. Winner advisers excluded from removal pool;later remaining denizens feed rebuild (site attachments remain saved).

questions.question: Explain Chronicle relic cleanup order, including Grand Scepter, losing relics, site refill and winner/Reliquary relics.
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Grand Scepter saved World Box. Losing players relics back relic deck and shuffle. Refill each faceup site to printed R count only if below,place facedown. Shuffle winner remaining held relics with Reliquary relics and put atop relic deck. Site refill precedes winner/Reliquary stacking.

Return losing relics to relic deck and shuffle.
Refill faceup sites below printed R count up to count, facedown.
Then shuffle winner’s remaining relics with Reliquary relics and stack atop relic deck.

questions.question: How are map cards and boards packed after Chronicle, and does the next group need the same players or status ownership?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Stack attached cards on each site;stack sites top Cradle on top,bottom Hinterland bottom,save World Box. Boards saved current Exile/Citizen sides. New people can join;non-Chancellors choose among saved boards in turn order unless group agrees reservations.

questions.question: A matching-suit card is played to a Homeland site after a different-suit card was discarded there this turn. Does reward trigger, what can reward be, and how is a relic reward resolved?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Yes provided no card of matching Homeland suit was discarded there this turn. Printed reward: favor or secret from matching bank/shared bank,or two warbands,or take site relic treating as Recover (no ordinary Recover action/site cost). Gain site-play favor then Homeland effect before When Played.

required_facts.expected_fact: Reward still triggers if no card of that Homeland’s matching suit was discarded at that site this turn.
Printed favor/secret from matching/shared bank, two warbands, or take site relic.
Treat relic reward as Recover without ordinary Supply/site resource cost.
Site-play favor first, then Homeland effect, then When Played.

questions.question: How do Coast sites change Travel and interact with Narrow Pass? Is it enough that destination alone is a Coast?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: From a Coast to another Coast costs one Supply and ignores Narrow Pass;both origin and destination required. Destination-only Coast uses normal costs/restrictions unless another effect applies.

required_facts.expected_fact: Origin and destination both Coasts: one Supply, ignore Narrow Pass.
Not enough; normal cost/restrictions apply absent another effect.
